answers.question: If `useVisit` in the OpenMRS frontend framework (openmrs-esm-core) changed its behaviour, which code in the patient chart app (openmrs-esm-patient-chart) uses it and could be affected?

paragraphs.text: `useVisit` is a React hook in the OpenMRS frontend framework that answers "where is this patient in their visit?" It is defined in the framework package `esm-react-utils` [1], and re-exported through `@openmrs/esm-framework`, which is how apps consume it. A "visit" in OpenMRS is a period during which a patient is seen at a facility; an "active visit" is the most recent visit with no end date.

In the patient chart app it is used in two ways: as a source of the active visit to render UI, and as a cache-mutation handle to refresh visit data after a change. Both would be affected by a behaviour change, but the mutation-based uses are the most fragile.

The hook returns `error`, `mutate`, `isValidating`, `activeVisit`, `isLoading`, plus two deprecated fields `currentVisit` and `currentVisitIsRetrospective` [2]. The `activeVisit` comes from one SWR call keyed with `includeInactive=false`, and `mutate` revalidates both that call and the retrospective-visit call [3]. It also writes into the visit context store when an active visit appears [4]. A test mock of the hook exists in the framework [5].
## Production code in patient-chart that depends on it

| Location | What it depends on |
| --- | --- |
| `patient-chart.resources.ts` | active visit, `isValidating`, `mutate` |
| `visit-tag.extension.tsx` | active visit + `isLoading` |
| `visit-attribute-tags.extension.tsx` | active visit attributes |
| `stop-visit.component.tsx` / `delete-visit.component.tsx` | presence of active visit |
| `end-visit-dialog.modal.tsx` | active visit + `mutate` |
| `visit-form.workspace.tsx` | `mutate` only |
| `exported-visit-form.workspace.tsx` | active visit conflict check + `isLoading` |

- **`usePatientChartPatientAndVisit`**, the hook that boots the patient chart, calls `useVisit` and reads `activeVisit`, `isValidating` and `mutate` [6]. It waits for both `isValidatingVisitContext` and `isValidatingActiveVisit` to be false before launching the workspace group, then sets the visit context and passes `mutateActiveVisit` in as `mutateVisitContext` [7]. This is the most sensitive consumer: a change to when `isValidating` turns false, or to what `mutate` refreshes, changes when workspaces launch, and the `mutate` function it hands to the chart store is the one every downstream component later calls.
- The `VisitTag` banner tag renders the blue "Active Visit" tag only when `!isLoading && activeVisit` [8].
- The visit-attribute tags extension filters `activeVisit?.attributes` against configured attribute types to render tags in the patient banner [9]; a change to the custom representation or to `activeVisit` would empty these tags.
- `StopVisitOverflowMenuItem` and `DeleteVisitOverflowMenuItem` show their banner-menu entries only when `activeVisit` is truthy [10] [11]. Delete additionally passes `activeVisit` into the delete dialog [12].
- `EndVisitDialog` reads `activeVisit` and `mutate`, calls `mutate()` after `updateVisit` succeeds, and clears the chart-store visit context if it matched [13].
- `VisitForm` uses only `mutate` to invalidate the active-visit cache after saving a visit [14].
- `exported-visit-form.workspace.tsx` uses `activeVisit` and `isLoading` to compute `hasActiveVisitConflict`, which blocks starting an overlapping visit unless configured to allow it [15].
## Indirect dependants: the `mutate` handle and SWR cache keys

`mutate` from `useVisit` is stored in the patient chart store as `mutateVisitContext` [16], and is called from the optimistic visit-mutations utilities [17] and [18]. So a behaviour change to `mutate` propagates to everything that mutates visit context through the store.

Separately, other code depends on the *exact URL shape* `useVisit` uses. `invalidateVisitHistory` and `invalidateCurrentVisit` in `revalidation-utils.ts` match cache keys by string, treating an `includeInactive=false` key as "current visit" and everything else as history [19] [20]. The same matching is hardcoded in the optimistic mutations [21]. If `useVisit` changed its URL or the `includeInactive` parameter, these invalidations would silently stop matching the hook's cache entry — the code would still compile, but refreshes would miss. The comments in `revalidation-utils.ts` even state the assumption: it exists to avoid revalidating "the 28+ components that use current visit data via the useVisit hook" [22].
## Tests that pin the current behaviour

These would fail if the returned shape changed: `patient-chart.resources.test.ts` [23], `visit-tag.test.tsx` [24], `stop-visit.test.tsx` [25], `delete-visit.test.tsx` [26], `end-visit-dialog.test.tsx` [27], `visit-form.test.tsx` [28], `visit-attribute-tags.test.tsx` [29], and `immunizations-detailed-summary.test.tsx`, which mocks `currentVisit` [30]. The deprecated `currentVisit` field is not read in any patient-chart production component I found — only tests and `postOrders.ts`, which takes a `currentVisit` parameter that is not sourced from the hook [31].

I only searched `openmrs-esm-patient-chart` and read the `useVisit` implementation in `openmrs-esm-core`; I did not check other selected repositories for consumers, so other apps may also depend on it. The specific "behaviour change" was not described, so the list above is by mechanism — data shape, URL keys, `isValidating` timing, `mutate` scope — rather than a per-change verdict. Uses reached through dynamic dispatch (extension slots registered in configuration rather than code) or through the `@openmrs/esm-framework` mock in apps not read here are not accounted for.
